frequency_question: How often do major partisan priority bills pass the U.S. Senate when subject to intense procedural friction and polarization within a single congressional term window?
membership_rule: Includes major partisan bills prioritized by congressional leadership that required overcoming procedural hurdles or filibuster-level opposition in the Senate between 1995 and 2026. Excludes routine appropriations, must-pass defense authorizations, and non-controversial bipartisan consensus measures.

cases.name: H.R. 1 / S. 1 For the People Act (2021)
Immigration and Border Security Reform Bills (2024)
American Health Care Act / Repeal Measures (2017)
Protecting the Right to Organize (PRO) Act (2021)
Bipartisan Infrastructure Law (2021 - bipartisan exception comparison)
Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (2017 - reconciliation exception)

coverage_note: 8 named major contested partisan votes representing the class; specialized procedural workarounds (reconciliation) account for the hits.
known_gaps: Does not fully separate standard legislative filibuster paths from budget reconciliation paths, though SAVE America Act requires overcoming standard procedural thresholds unless attached to must-pass vehicles.
skeleton: Total major contested partisan bills attempted versus successfully passing the Senate cloture threshold or reconciliation limits in modern highly polarized congresses (114th to 118th Congresses).
multiplier: 2 hits out of 8 benchmarked major contested structural bills = 25%
validity_reason: Senate procedural rules (the filibuster and cloture requirements) remain stable on this time horizon unless structural rules are altered.
